sections.notes:
I checked the study guide: "Skills measured as of July 20, 2026" is confirmed, and the 2.2 bullets match the prompt. All 10 source URLs load and are official and current. Each one supports its card, including the right fact given in the explanations of the false cards:
- 01: autoscale overview: "you can configure autoscale rules to increase and decrease the number of virtual machines".
- 02: "Availability sets distribute VMs across multiple fault domains" and "assigns an update domain and a fault domain to each virtual machine".
- 06: ACI runs containers "without having to adopt a higher-level service"; AKS appears only through optional virtual nodes.
- 07: Functions: "Process message queues using Azure Queue Storage, Service Bus, or Event Hubs".
- 08: "Peerings by themselves aren't transitive ... There's no connectivity between VirtualNetwork1 and VirtualNetwork3 through VirtualNetwork2".
- 09: ExpressRoute "Traffic never traverses the public internet"; VPN Gateway is an "Encrypted IPsec/IKE tunnel over the public internet".
- 10: private endpoint: "a network interface that uses a private IP address from your virtual network".

I found no wrong answers. The section is balanced: 5 true and 5 false, average statement length 91.6 (true) vs 93.2 (false). Difficulty mix: 4 easy, 4 medium, 2 hard. No duplicates with other sections; the only nearby cards are 1.1-10 (serverless) and 3.4-10 (Application Insights), which rest on different facts.

Borderline cards I did not flag:
- 01 (scale sets need an operator to add each VM) is close to a strawman, because autoscale is what scale sets are known for. It is still defensible, since manual scaling is the default mode.
- 05 (App Service hosts web apps and REST APIs) is an easy definitional true card. A stronger option would be "Azure App Service can run a web app deployed as a custom container image." (source: "if your app is containerized, you can just deploy it as a custom container").
- 08 is worded awkwardly ("connects their other peered networks to each other"). It is false under every reading, but "Peering VNet A with B and B with C lets A reach C through B." would be clearer.
- 09's false statement has two wrong parts ("encrypted" and "public internet"). The public-internet part is the decisive one, so it holds up.

Coverage gap: the guide's 2.2 bullets name Azure DNS and public endpoints, and no 2.2 card tests either. Consider using a replacement slot for Azure DNS, for example that it hosts DNS domains but cannot be used to buy domain names.

Balance: the section is 5 true / 5 false and stays so with the suggested fixes, because the replacement for 05 is true and the replacement for 09 is false. No retired products or old names appear. No duplicates against 3.1 or 3.3: s3.1-05 (pricing calculator) does not mirror s3.4-02 (Advisor).

duplicates.why: Both test the same CapEx/OpEx split. 1.1-07 (upfront servers are OpEx, false) and 1.1-08 (consumption spending is OpEx, true) are two sides of one two-way distinction. Knowing either answer gives you the other. 1.1-08 is the weaker card: it hedges with 'generally' and is close to a truism.

Both rest on one fact: an Azure Policy assignment applies to its own scope and its children, and does not reach up or sideways. 2.1-10's explanation ('Policy inheritance flows down the hierarchy') answers 3.2-05 outright. 3.2-05 is the weaker card and close to a strawman, because few learners would expect a resource-group assignment to reach sibling groups.

conflictGroups.name: capex-opex
conflictGroups.why: A mirrored pair on the CapEx/OpEx distinction, one true and one false. Use this group if neither card is dropped.

conflictGroups.name: consumption-pricing
conflictGroups.why: 1.2-06's explanation says cloud charges vary with consumption, and 1.1-08 says spending follows consumption. Both give away 1.1-09 (pay-as-you-go is metered use, not forecast traffic).

conflictGroups.name: provider-physical-layer
conflictGroups.why: 1.3-04's explanation says the provider maintains the underlying physical network, which answers 1.1-02 (the customer does not maintain physical hosts). 1.1-02's explanation in turn frames 1.3-04's virtual-versus-physical boundary.

conflictGroups.name: iaas-paas-os-boundary
conflictGroups.why: 1.3-06's explanation ('the provider manages the underlying platform') gives away 1.3-05. 1.3-05 (in PaaS the provider maintains the OS) set against 1.3-01 (in IaaS the provider patches the guest OS) is a mirrored OS-ownership pair. 1.3-01's explanation also says the IaaS customer maintains the OS.

conflictGroups.name: saas-responsibility
conflictGroups.why: All three test where the SaaS line falls. 1.3-10's explanation (SaaS delivers a complete application with less customer control) points to 1.3-08. 1.3-08 against 1.3-09 is a near-mirror ('the provider maintains X' true, 'the provider sets Y' false).

conflictGroups.name: management-interfaces
conflictGroups.why: 1.2-10's explanation lists command-line interfaces, APIs and PowerShell, which confirms 3.3-03 and 3.3-04. 1.2-10 ('requires a web portal') and 3.3-02 ('requires a locally installed terminal') also share one 'requires interface X' false template.

conflictGroups.name: scale-out-instances
conflictGroups.why: 2.2-01's statement and explanation describe scaling by adding VM instances, which tells the player that scaling out adds instances (1.2-02 is false).

conflictGroups.name: region-datacenter
conflictGroups.why: 2.1-02 (a region groups datacenters) and 2.1-01's explanation (you pick a region, not a datacenter) give each other away.

conflictGroups.name: scope-inheritance-downward
conflictGroups.why: All three are false because an assignment is said to reach up or sideways in the hierarchy. 2.1-10's explanation ('inheritance flows down') settles the other two.

conflictGroups.name: storage-redundancy
conflictGroups.why: 2.3-06's explanation says GRS keeps locally redundant copies in the primary region and GZRS uses zones, which hints at LRS (2.3-04) and ZRS (2.3-05). 2.3-05's statement (ZRS = zones) also makes 'GRS uses zones' (2.3-06) easy to reject.

conflictGroups.name: blob-tier-online-offline
conflictGroups.why: Mirrored pair. Cool is online with immediate reads (true), archive gives immediate reads (false). Each explanation contrasts online with offline/rehydration and so answers the other card.

conflictGroups.name: blob-vs-files
conflictGroups.why: 2.3-09 pairs file shares with Azure Files and Windows Server, which hints that Blob Storage does not expose SMB shares (2.3-01). 2.3-01's explanation names Azure Files as the SMB service.

conflictGroups.name: rbac-owns-permissions
conflictGroups.why: Both use the same false template, a service (Conditional Access or Azure Policy) given RBAC's job of granting or editing permissions. 3.2-07's explanation says RBAC grants permissions, which reveals 2.4-06.

conflictGroups.name: policy-compliance-not-permission
conflictGroups.why: 3.2-07's explanation ('Azure Policy governs resource compliance') answers 3.2-03, and 3.2-03's statement makes 3.2-07 easy to reject.

conflictGroups.name: beyond-azure-scope
conflictGroups.why: A repeated 'does the service work outside Azure?' pattern, and it always resolves to yes. The Azure-only versions (Defender for Cloud, Application Insights) are false, and the multicloud/on-premises versions (Purview, Arc) are true. Seeing one teaches the pattern for the rest.

conflictGroups.name: cost-management-alerts
conflictGroups.why: 3.1-07's explanation (budgets 'can trigger threshold alerts') shows that Cost Management alerts on spend, which makes 3.1-08 an easy true.

conflictGroups.name: cost-grouping
conflictGroups.why: Both are true cards with the same template, 'costs can be grouped by X' (subscription/RG, then tag/cost center). One primes the other.

conflictGroups.name: purview-catalog
conflictGroups.why: Both are about what the Purview Data Map catalog holds. 3.2-01's 'catalog data sources' framing, together with 3.2-02's explanation (scans ingest metadata), makes the pair answer each other.

conflictGroups.name: resource-locks
conflictGroups.why: 3.2-09's explanation ('even for users with broad Azure RBAC permissions') gives away 3.2-08 (a Delete lock also stops an Owner). 3.2-09's statement ('blocks control-plane updates') against 3.2-10 ('blocks data-plane writes') is a mirrored control-plane/data-plane pair, and 3.2-10's explanation states the control-plane scope.

conflictGroups.name: arm-template-format
conflictGroups.why: 3.3-09's explanation ('converts a Bicep file to an ARM JSON template') answers 3.3-08 (ARM templates are JSON). 3.3-06's explanation (templates declare resources) overlaps 3.3-08's 'resource definitions' wording.

conflictGroups.name: advisor-existing-resources
conflictGroups.why: 3.4-01's explanation ('analyzes deployed Azure resources') directly answers 3.4-02 (cost recommendations for planned VMs is false).

conflictGroups.name: health-views
conflictGroups.why: A mirrored pair: Service Health is personalized (3.4-03 true) and Azure status is subscription-filtered (3.4-04 false). 3.4-04's explanation names Service Health as the subscription-specific view. 3.4-05 (Resource Health per resource) completes the global/subscription/resource ladder and is easy to infer from the other two.

conflictGroups.name: log-analytics
conflictGroups.why: 3.4-07's explanation (logs go to a Log Analytics workspace 'where Azure Monitor can analyze them') primes 3.4-08 (Log Analytics queries Azure Monitor log data).

scan.tells:
Length is not a tell. Overall true statements average 84.0 characters and false ones 82.6. Every section is within 5 characters (largest gap 4.4 in 1.2, then 3.2 in 3.3), and every section is 5 true / 5 false. The exploitable tells are in the wording:

(1) Hedge verbs predict true. 'can' appears in 23 statements: 21 true, 2 false (2.3-01, 2.3-03). 'supports' 4/4 true, 'lets' 2/2 true, 'reports' 2/2 true. Altogether 29 of 31 hedged statements are true.

(2) 'requires/require' predicts false: 8/8 false (1.1-04, 1.1-10, 1.2-10, 2.2-01, 2.2-06, 3.3-02, 3.4-06, 3.4-10). These are all one template, 'X requires Y' where Y is optional.

(3) 'each' predicts false: 7/7 false (1.2-06, 1.3-09, 2.2-01, 2.2-03, 2.2-08, 3.1-10, 3.3-06).

(4) Overreach adverbs predict false. 'automatically' 2/2 false (3.1-07, 3.1-10), 'by default' 1/1 false (3.4-09), 'directly' 2/2 false (3.2-08, 3.3-09), 'also' 1/1 false (2.2-08), 'independently' 1/1 false (3.1-02). Only 1.2-09 ('automatic replacement') breaks the pattern. 'grants' is 3/3 false (2.4-07, 2.4-08, 3.2-07).

(5) Any statement containing 'customer' is false: 5/5 (1.1-02, 1.3-01, 1.3-04, 1.3-06, 1.3-09). In 1.3, 'the provider does something to the customer's X' is false 4/4, and 'the provider maintains the platform/updates' is true 2/2.

(6) A recurring false template credits a service with its twin's job. 8 cards, all false: 2.2-09 (ExpressRoute = VPN), 2.3-01 (Blob = Files SMB), 2.3-08 (AzCopy = Storage Explorer GUI), 2.3-10 (Data Box = Migrate), 2.4-01 (Entra ID = Domain Services), 2.4-06 (Conditional Access = RBAC), 3.2-07 (Policy = RBAC), 3.4-04 (Azure status = Service Health). No true card uses the same shape, so 'service named with a sibling's well-known job' always means false. The prompt banned repeated distractor templates.

(7) Scope reaching up or sideways is always false: 2.1-10, 2.4-07, 3.2-05 (plus 2.1-08 and 3.1-10 on scope confinement and inheritance), 5/5 false.

(8) Azure-only versus beyond-Azure: restricting a Microsoft service to Azure is false 2/2 (2.4-10, 3.4-10), and extending one beyond Azure is true 2/2 (3.2-01, 3.3-05).

(9) 'one/single uniform...' framed as a restriction is false (1.2-01, 2.1-08, 3.3-01). 'one/single' as a plain description is true (2.1-02, 2.1-07, 2.3-04, 2.3-05, 2.4-02), so this tell is weaker.

A player who answers 'can/supports/lets → True; requires/each/automatically/directly/customer/role-swap → False' gets about 60 of 110 cards right without any Azure knowledge.

Side quality notes, not part of the tell counts:
- Truism or near-truism risk: 1.1-01 (definition of cloud computing), 2.2-04 (a VM uses a NIC to join a subnet), 1.2-07 (providers 'can help' against DDoS).
- Strawman risk: 1.2-08 (templates 'primarily forecast cost'), 3.2-05 (sibling resource groups), 2.1-01 (awkward wording, 'datacenters are selected as deployment locations').
- 1.2-03 and 1.2-09 sit close to the generic 'the cloud lets you scale/recover' truisms the prompt warns about.
- 3.3-10 is true but incomplete: ARM deployments also target management groups and tenants. That is acceptable because 'can target' does not claim the list is exhaustive.
